tagline: A mile and a half of moss-hung oaks, then the waterway.
intro: Airlie Road leaves US 76 at Military Cutoff Road in Wilmington and runs a mile and a half under tall pines and oaks hung with Spanish moss. Near the end the canopy opens all at once onto marsh grass, boat docks and the Atlantic Intracoastal Waterway, and the byway stops at the Wrightsville Beach drawbridge. The whole drive takes about five minutes.
The road is named for Airlie Gardens, laid out in 1886 as a private garden for the Pembroke Jones family and named for the family's home in Scotland. New Hanover County bought it in 1999.

moments.title: Airlie Gardens
moments.text: Inside the gates stands the Airlie Oak, a southern live oak reckoned at 500 years old and measured in 2007 as the largest live oak in North Carolina.

moments.title: Minnie Evans Bottle Chapel
moments.text: Minnie Evans kept the Airlie gate from 1948 to 1974 and hung her paintings on it to sell, and after her death local artists built her a chapel of reused glass bottles.

moments.title: Wrightsville Beach
moments.text: Past the drawbridge lies Wrightsville Beach, a 4.6-mile island that in the 1700s and 1800s could be reached only by boat.
